title: Tibber Energy dashboard records large negative consumption around midnight
body: After updating to Home Assistant 2021.12.0 late last night, my Energy dashboard shows large negative consumption around midnight for all my meters. I have no energy production, so this is clearly wrong. It happens on both a Supervised installation and a Home Assistant OS installation. The last working Core version was 2021.11.5, and I cannot see anything useful in the logs.

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant 2021.12.0, all my meters show large negative consumption around midnight even though I have no energy production.
I see the same behavior on both my Supervised and Home Assistant OS installations.
N0.label: N0 negative midnight consumption reported

symptoms_visible: The Energy dashboard records a large negative entry around each midnight while my Tibber accumulated-consumption sensor rises during the day and starts a new daily cycle.
The negative entry is approximately the amount consumed during the previous day.
N1.label: N1 Tibber daily-reset pattern established

symptoms_visible: The Tibber accumulated-consumption value starts a new daily cycle around midnight, and the Energy dashboard records a negative amount approximately equal to the preceding day's total.
N2.label: N2 metadata regression identified

symptoms_visible: Using the last-meter-consumption sensor removes the negative value on a setup where that sensor exists, but the hourly consumption is shifted by about an hour.
Some Tibber installations do not expose a last-meter-consumption sensor at all.
N2_x.label: N2_x last-meter workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The replacement sensor does not provide a satisfactory Energy dashboard: it is unavailable on some systems and its hourly values can appear one hour late.
N2b.label: N2b workaround rejected and metadata regression identified

symptoms_visible: After applying the Tibber patch and restarting Home Assistant, the first hour shows a large positive consumption spike.
Later hours look normal, and the statistics database now contains a reset timestamp for the sensor.
N3.label: N3 candidate reset-marker patch installed

symptoms_visible: With the patched Tibber integration, midnight passes without the large negative consumption entry.
The completed daily Energy total matches the accumulated-consumption value at midnight.
N4.label: N4 candidate fix verified across midnight

symptoms_visible: The Tibber accumulated-consumption sensor crosses midnight without creating a large negative Energy entry, and the daily total remains correct.
N_terminal.label: terminal Tibber midnight statistics resolved

question_patterns: Which entity is configured as the consumption source in the Energy dashboard?
Which integration and sensor provide these meter readings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using Tibber data, specifically sensor.accumulated_consumption_xxx, as the Energy dashboard input. Other affected Tibber users see the same thing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: These are non-resetting hardware meter-total entities from a different integration; Tibber is not installed.
I use the same Tibber accumulated-consumption entity but have only one meter.

question_patterns: What does the source sensor itself do around the time the negative entry appears?
Does the source meter decrease gradually, or does it start a new cycle each day?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The accumulated-consumption sensor rises through the day and starts over around midnight. It is not showing actual negative consumption.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The source sensor itself drops to a large negative value and stays negative for the rest of the day.

question_patterns: Did this happen only when Home Assistant was updated or restarted?
Does the negative entry repeat on subsequent nights?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I updated at about 22:30 on 11 December, but the large negative value repeated around the next midnight without another update. So it is not caused just by the act of updating.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It happened only once at the exact moment I upgraded and never appeared at another midnight.

question_patterns: How does the size of the negative entry compare with the previous day's consumption?
Is there a recognizable relationship between the negative amount and the daily total?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The incorrect negative amount is approximately the previous day's total consumption; for example, about 17 kWh used yesterday appears as roughly -17 kWh in the first hour today.

edges.comment: Opening reporter plus c0-c5: the reporter identifies Tibber in c1, while several affected Tibber users establish the same daily-reset pattern. Their compatible observations are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you compare the entity's current statistics metadata with the last working release?
What changed in the accumulated-consumption entity's metadata in the affected update?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The linked change replaced total_increasing with total for Tibber accumulated consumption and production. Before 2021.12 this sensor was treated as total_increasing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The entity metadata is identical in 2021.11.5 and 2021.12.0; it is still total_increasing in both.
The same metadata change is present, but I first observed it after updating directly from an earlier 2021.11 patch release.

edges.comment: c6 and c15-c22: affected users inspect the linked change and identify that accumulated consumption changed from total_increasing to total. The maintainer's explanation about hourly corrections is not put into the simulated user's answer; it remains engineer-side information on the consuming solution.

solution.intent: Replace the Tibber accumulated-consumption entity in the Energy dashboard with the last-meter-consumption entity.
solution.concrete_example: Select sensor.last_meter_consumption_xxx as the Energy dashboard consumption source instead of sensor.accumulated_consumption_xxx.

edges.comment: c9-c12 and c52-c57: one affected setup removes the negative entry by switching sensors, but other affected users lack that entity and users who have it observe approximately one-hour-shifted hourly data. This is therefore a real but unsatisfactory workaround, not the fix for the opening Tibber accumulated-consumption regression.

question_patterns: Can you compare the original accumulated entity's statistics metadata with the last working release?
What metadata change accompanied the regression in the affected update?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The accumulated-consumption entity changed from total_increasing to total in 2021.12.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The original accumulated-consumption entity did not change state class between the working and affected releases.

edges.comment: Recovery from the c9/c52 workaround: affected users return attention to the original accumulated-consumption entity and identify the metadata change discussed in c15-c22.

solution.intent: Keep Tibber accumulated consumption as a total that permits corrections, but record the genuine daily cycle boundary when the value drops during the midnight hour.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the Tibber sensor so accumulated consumption and production retain total semantics, parse the measurement timestamp, and set the reset timestamp when the new value is below the previous value during hour 0. Restart Home Assistant, expect that introducing reset metadata may disturb the first statistics interval, and test the setup across midnight.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer establishes that Tibber can make small hourly downward corrections, so strictly increasing semantics are not the accepted final diagnosis. Combining that fact with the daily reset pattern and the state-class change shows why total semantics need an explicit reset boundary: without it, statistics interpret the midnight drop as negative consumption.

edges.comment: c19, c22, c29-c32 and c36-c40: the maintainer proposes reset-boundary handling, and the reporter manually patches sensor.py and keeps that patched installation for testing. This persistent local code change creates system state S2. The maintainer's hourly-correction fact and the causal reading are engineer-side inferences, not simulated-user answers.

solution.intent: Return to the Tibber accumulated-consumption source and apply reset-boundary handling instead of relying on the unavailable or time-shifted replacement sensor.
solution.concrete_example: Re-select sensor.accumulated_consumption_xxx, apply the Tibber sensor change that records its genuine daily reset, restart Home Assistant, and leave it running through midnight.
solution.inference_hint: The replacement sensor's hourly offset is a separate timestamping issue. The opening regression is addressed at the original accumulated-consumption entity by distinguishing its daily reset from ordinary value corrections.

edges.comment: Recovery route combining c9-c12/c52-c57 with c32-c42: after the alternate sensor proves unsatisfactory, the affected-user side restores accumulated consumption and tests the maintainer's patch.

question_patterns: Please leave the patched setup running through midnight and tell me what the Energy dashboard shows afterward.
After the next daily cycle change, do you still get the large negative entry?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Midnight passed without incident. Apart from the one initial bump after I introduced the patch, there was no large negative consumption entry.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same large negative amount appeared again at midnight with the patched setup.
There was no negative midnight entry, but the daily reset occurred a few seconds after midnight.

question_patterns: After a complete day, how does the Energy dashboard total compare with the Tibber accumulated value?
Can you compare the completed daily total against the sensor value at midnight?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Energy dashboard total for the completed day is exactly the Tibber Pulse accumulated-consumption value at midnight. A second affected setup also crossed midnight without the negative spike.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The negative spike is gone, but the completed Energy total is missing most of the day's consumption.

edges.comment: c42-c47: the reporter confirms the candidate on their own patched installation after midnight, and participant10 independently confirms no midnight spike and an exact match between the Energy total and the accumulated value. The affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Adopt the verified Tibber reset-boundary handling so accumulated consumption remains usable by the Energy dashboard without interpreting its daily reset as negative usage.
solution.concrete_example: Ship the tested Tibber sensor behavior that retains total semantics for corrected accumulated readings and records the midnight daily reset. The reporter's overnight test showed no negative spike and a correct daily total; the one-time spike seen when introducing the metadata may require statistics cleanup but is not the recurring midnight failure.

edges.comment: Resolution chain from c32-c50: the reset-boundary implementation was tested on affected users' own systems and accepted as the fix. Later discussion about last-meter timestamps and the separate cost graph is not part of the opening negative-consumption problem.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: after Tibber accumulated consumption changed from total_increasing to total, its daily reset lacked the reset-boundary handling needed by Energy statistics, so the midnight drop was counted as negative consumption approximately equal to the prior day's total.

Must preserve total-style semantics rather than simply force the sensor back to strictly increasing behavior, because the Tibber accumulated value can receive ordinary downward corrections as well as its daily reset.
The fix must record the genuine daily reset boundary for Tibber accumulated consumption and production while keeping the original accumulated-consumption sensor usable in the Energy dashboard.
Must not present sensor.last_meter_consumption_xxx as the general fix: it is unavailable on some Tibber setups and can produce approximately one-hour-shifted hourly values.
Must ground resolution in an affected user's overnight verification: no negative entry appears at midnight and the completed Energy total matches the accumulated-consumption value.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Home Assistant user who can inspect statistics in SQLite, edit an integration file manually, restart Core, compare sensor metadata, and test a patch overnight.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, analytical, and cooperative; supplies graphs and database observations, explains timing concerns, and reports intermediate side effects before confirming an overnight result.
